report.title: Inventory deploy d-4840 introduced null access causing InventoryReservationFailed and increased checkout errors since 2026-11-27T17:32Z
report.summary: Since ~2026-11-27T17:32Z checkout-api error rate rose to ~15-16% driven by inventory reservation failures. A deploy to inventory-service (d-4840) at 2026-11-27T17:31Z changed warehouse routing and introduced a null access bug.
report.customerImpact: Customers are seeing failed checkouts (~16% error rate) starting at 2026-11-27T17:32Z because checkout-api cannot reserve inventory; payments are unaffected. This prevents order completion for affected carts.

rootCause.description: Deploy d-4840 modified ReservationService to set warehouse = item.Variant.WarehouseCode ?? defaultWarehouse. Accessing item.Variant before the null-coalescing operator can NRE when Variant is null, causing InventoryReservationFailed errors which propagate to checkout-api and increase error rate.

evidence.detail: checkout-api error_rate rose from baseline 0.003 to latest 0.1584 (change detected startedAt 2026-11-27T17:32Z). inventory-service error_rate rose from 0.001 to 0.168 (startedAt 2026-11-27T17:32Z).
Deploy d-4840 (inventory-service v5.1.0) deployed at 2026-11-27T17:31Z by dokafor with summary 'Route bundle and variant items to their own warehouse'.
Deploy diff for d-4840 shows change: replaced 'var warehouse = defaultWarehouse;' with 'var warehouse = item.Variant.WarehouseCode ?? defaultWarehouse;' (src/Inventory/ReservationService.cs).

87 ERROR logs in checkout-api from 2026-11-27T17:32Z to 2026-11-27T18:00Z with pattern 'checkout failed orderId=<orderId> step=reserve error=InventoryReservationFailed' (samples at 17:54–18:00Z). First seen at 2026-11-27T17:32Z matching metrics and deploy timing.

recommendedActions.rationale: Revert the failing change to restore previous reservation behavior quickly; timestamps show errors started within 1 minute after this deploy.
If deploy rolled out gradually, pause further rollouts to stop propagation while rollback or fix proceeds.

Prepare a hotfix changing assignment to safely access Variant, e.g. 'var warehouse = (item.Variant != null ? item.Variant.WarehouseCode : defaultWarehouse);' and add unit tests for items without Variant. Deploy after rollback or to canary with tight monitoring.
Confirm rollback or fix reduces error rates back to baseline (error_rate <1%). Watch for duplicate reservations or other side-effects.

followUps: Add unit/integration tests covering CartItem with null Variant and bundle/variant routing scenarios.
Consider code review checklist to avoid null dereference in similar changes; add static analysis or enable nullable annotations.
Verify no orders were double-charged (payment-service metrics show provider_error_rate unchanged) and reconcile any partial orders.
